subject: Clarify responsibility for customer-managed network latency — proposed exception
messages:
From: Carlos Ramirez <carlos.ramirez@novapath.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novapath.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment readiness — network ownership question

Hi Soojin / Kimberly,

Quick follow up from our on-site last week: our infra team identified several spikes in request tail latency that appear to correlate with a firewall queue on our edge routers. We run the edge NAT and peering in our colo; Redwood is serving model inference in our private VPC.

Novapath is asking for an SLA note to clarify that latency outside the Reedwood-managed fabric (customer-controlled edge routing / firewalling) is excluded from Redwood's latency SLOs, and to capture what evidence we should provide if we request an attribution. To move forward with the Dedicated/Private purchase we need this spelled out — legal will want specific language we can sign.

Can Redwood provide a short exception clause and a list of telemetry/artifacts that'll satisfy an attribution review?

Thanks,
Carlos
Senior Platform Lead, Novapath

---
Attachments: novapath_network_traces_oct20.zip (archive, 12 MB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ramirez <carlos.ramirez@novapath.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment readiness — network ownership question

Carlos — thanks for the note and for the traces.

High level: we can accept a narrow operational carve-out for customer-managed edge routing and customer NAT/firewall queuing in the Private contract, but we need: (1) unambiguous clause text, (2) a reproducible evidence protocol (what logs/traces are required), and (3) a fallback policy (how traffic will fail over or degrade) so customer applications can decide critical-path behavior.

I've drafted a lean exception clause and compiled a checklist of telemetry we typically require. Draft attached (redwood_proposed_sla_exception_draft.pdf). The checklist includes:
- pcap or flow logs showing end-to-end RTT skewed at the customer's edge
- timestamps and request IDs from Redwood ingress with full KV-cache timestamps
- colo / edge device syslogs showing queue/drop events
- BGP/peering metrics if relevant

Next steps I propose:
1) We review the draft clause with Novapath legal (1x call, 30 min).
2) Novapath provides one representative full trace and the edge syslog we can jointly analyze.
3) Redwood and Novapath agree on a 3rd-party forensic step if attribution remains unclear.

Kimberly / Marcus — can you review the clause and confirm whether the proposed evidence checklist is sufficient operationally? I want to ensure we don't accidentally require data we can't produce from our side (e.g., internal kernel traces).

Best,
Soojin
Sr. Manager, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment readiness — network ownership question

Soojin — quick read and looks sensible. A couple of operational clarifications:

- For evidence we need request IDs with tokenization timestamps + ingress egress timestamps from our side. That is standard and we can produce via the Console (per-route tracing).
- We should explicitly exclude 3xx/4xx application errors that manifest as client timeouts at the edge — those are not Redwood's transmission responsibility unless our logs show server-side queuing.
- Marcus, on the forensics point: suggest we add an escalation path to our Network Reliability team and an SLO "attribution review" SLA (48 hours for initial analysis) so Novapath has SLAs on the investigation timelines.

I'll propose edits inline on the PDF and upload a redline.

Kimberly
Director, Enterprise Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment readiness — network ownership question

Hi all — quick operational addendum from the runtime side.

Two practical notes to include in the clause and checklist:
1) Timestamp canonicalization: we'll require request IDs where timestamps are in UTC and include the Redwood ingress microsecond marker. This prevents clock skew from invalidating evidence.
2) KV-cache warmup / cold miss noise: if a spike coincides with cache cold starts we will note that as a Redwood cause unless Novapath can show simultaneous edge packet loss. Include a short example in the playbook so both teams can spot it.

Also supporting Kimberly's idea of a 48-hour attribution review window. We should be explicit about who funds a 3rd-party packet forensics step — typical is the customer pays unless Redwood's logs show clear server-side queuing.

I'll add text for the timestamp canonicalization and a sample artifact template.

Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Our legal team reviewed the draft and proposed two small changes: (1) clarify that the customer will provide the initial evidence within 10 business days of an incident request, and (2) a mutual agreement window of 5 business days before a third-party forensics step is engaged. Both seem reasonable.

Operationally, we attached a sample full-trace from last week's incident. We've redacted internal IPs but left request IDs and syslog entries. Please confirm whether this trace is enough to trigger an attribution review.

Carlos

Carlos / team — thanks for the trace and the legal feedback. Confirming next steps so we have a clear mutual action plan: 

1) Redwood accepts a narrow exception for customer-controlled edge routing/firewall queuing. Final clause will include: (i) required artifacts (our evidence template), (ii) a 10 business-day window for the customer to provide initial evidence, (iii) a 5 business-day discovery/mutual-agreement window prior to a paid 3rd-party forensics step, and (iv) a 48-hour attribution-review SLA from Redwood's Network Reliability team.

2) Novapath to upload the redacted trace you've provided into the shared Drive link and confirm the request IDs. We'll run an initial analysis and respond within 48 hours.

3) Marcus / Neha: Marcus will author the timestamp canonicalization paragraph and example artifact. Neha, can you confirm that the evidence template does not request PII or keys (we must avoid asking for KMS materials)? Please flag anything that looks like secret material.

4) Legal / Contract: Redwood legal will prepare an addendum with the final clause for signature; we'll aim for a one-week turnaround after the minor redline.

I'll set up a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the draft with Novapath legal — tentative 09:00 PT.

Thanks all — good progress.

Soojin
Sr. Manager, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
